blockers.title: SEVP-certification of school not confirmed
blockers.user_message: Only SEVP-certified schools can issue an I-20. Verify the school yourself — agents sometimes push non-SEVP or low-credibility schools that wreck your 214(b) case.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Verify your school is SEVP-certified at studyinthestates.dhs.gov before proceeding.
blockers.rule_source_name: Must Be Accepted at an SEVP-Certified School

blockers.title: Form I-20 not yet received
blockers.user_message: The I-20 (Certificate of Eligibility) is issued by the school's DSO after you're entered in SEVIS. No I-20 = no F-1 application.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Contact your school's DSO to obtain your I-20. The visa application cannot proceed without it.
blockers.rule_source_name: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current

blockers.title: Form I-20 is not fully signed
blockers.user_message: An unsigned I-20 is invalid. Sign it and confirm the DSO signature is present.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Confirm both the DSO signature and your own signature are present on the I-20 before applying.
blockers.rule_source_name: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current

blockers.title: School on I-20 does not match visa application
blockers.user_message: For your first US entry the school on the visa must match the I-20. If you change schools before the visa, get an updated visa.
blockers.recommended_next_step: If you changed schools, obtain an updated I-20 from the new school before applying.
blockers.rule_source_name: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current

blockers.title: SEVIS I-901 fee not paid
blockers.user_message: The SEVIS fee (USD 350 for F-1) must be paid BEFORE the visa is issued. Pay only at fmjfee.com — beware fake payment sites pushed by agents. No paid fee on record = refusal on the day, no same-day fix.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Pay the USD 350 SEVIS fee at fmjfee.com before your interview. No payment = refusal on the day.
blockers.rule_source_name: SEVIS I-901 Fee Must Be Paid Before Visa Is Issued

blockers.title: SEVIS ID on fee receipt does not match I-20
blockers.user_message: Pay using the exact SEVIS ID on your I-20. A mismatch means the system can't confirm your payment at the interview.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Ensure you paid using the exact SEVIS ID on your I-20. A mismatch prevents fee confirmation at interview.
blockers.rule_source_name: SEVIS I-901 Fee Must Be Paid Before Visa Is Issued

blockers.title: DS-160 online application not completed
blockers.user_message: The DS-160 is mandatory before the interview. Complete it carefully — it is the spine of your case and everything you say at interview must match it.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Complete the DS-160 at ceac.state.gov before your interview. It is a mandatory step.
blockers.rule_source_name: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent

blockers.title: DS-160 confirmation barcode page not printed
blockers.user_message: Bring the printed DS-160 confirmation barcode page to the interview. Without it you can be turned away.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Print the DS-160 confirmation page including the barcode and bring it to your interview.
blockers.rule_source_name: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent

blockers.title: Social media handles not fully disclosed on DS-160
blockers.user_message: List every platform/handle from the last 5 years, including inactive ones. Omitting an account is a ground for denial and a possible bar.
blockers.recommended_next_step: List every social media account used in the last 5 years on the DS-160. Any omission is a ground for denial.
blockers.rule_source_name: Social Media Must Be Public and Fully Disclosed (From June 18, 2025)

blockers.title: Social media profiles not set to public
blockers.user_message: Since 18 Jun 2025, F/M/J applicants must make all profiles public for vetting. No official deadline is specified, so set them public before submitting and keep them public until a decision is made.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Set all social media profiles to public before applying. This has been required for F/M/J applicants since 18 June 2025.
blockers.rule_source_name: Social Media Must Be Public and Fully Disclosed (From June 18, 2025)

blockers.title: Unable to demonstrate ties to Pakistan (214(b) risk)
blockers.user_message: 214(b) is the #1 refusal ground for Pakistani F-1 applicants. The officer PRESUMES you intend to immigrate; you must overcome it with a credible, specific return story — in seconds, verbally.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Identify and document concrete ties to Pakistan before proceeding. Without them, a 214(b) refusal is very likely.
blockers.rule_source_name: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)

blockers.title: Visa interview not yet booked
blockers.user_message: An interview is required for most applicants 14-79. Book early; wait times vary. 2025-2026 vetting can add 221(g) administrative processing.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Book your interview at the US Embassy or Consulate. An interview is required for most F-1 applicants aged 14–79.
blockers.rule_source_name: Visa Interview at US Embassy/Consulate Required

blockers.title: Core interview documents not fully assembled
blockers.user_message: Assemble the full set before the day. Missing a core document can end the interview before it starts.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Assemble all required documents: valid passport, I-20, DS-160 confirmation, SEVIS receipt, and financial evidence.
blockers.rule_source_name: Visa Interview at US Embassy/Consulate Required

blockers.title: Financial evidence may not cover full I-20 cost
blockers.user_message: The US sets no fixed figure — you must cover the total cost of attendance stated on YOUR I-20, plus return travel, without unauthorized work. Underfunding is a top 214(b) refusal cause.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Ensure your financial evidence covers the full cost of attendance on your I-20 plus return travel.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Prior immigration history may not be fully disclosed on DS-160
blockers.user_message: Failing to disclose a prior refusal or violation on DS-160 is misrepresentation — a permanent-bar risk far worse than the refusal itself.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Disclose all prior refusals and immigration violations accurately on the DS-160.
blockers.rule_source_name: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed

blockers.title: Passport validity may be insufficient (under 6 months beyond stay)
blockers.user_message: Renew before applying if needed. An insufficiently valid passport blocks visa issuance.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Renew your passport before applying so it is valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended US stay.
blockers.rule_source_name: Passport Must Be Valid 6+ Months Beyond Intended Stay

blockers.title: Document authenticity not confirmed
blockers.user_message: Fabricated bank balances, fake experience letters, or altered transcripts cause refusal AND a permanent misrepresentation bar — even if an agent did it in your name. Verify every document.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Personally verify every document in your application. Remove or replace any document that may be false or altered.
blockers.rule_source_name: Application Integrity and Agent Risk

blockers.title: I-20 details may not be consistent with other documents
blockers.user_message: Mismatches between the I-20, DS-160, admission letter, and financial papers are a classic Pakistani refusal trigger. Cross-check name spelling, funding amount, program, and dates.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Cross-check all I-20 details — personal information, programme, funding — against your DS-160, admission letter, and financial papers.
blockers.rule_source_name: Form I-20 Mandatory — Must Be Signed and Current

blockers.title: DS-160 not personally reviewed by the applicant
blockers.user_message: Agents sometimes enter wrong job titles, hide refusals, or inflate funding on your DS-160. You are bound by what's submitted in your name — and asked about it under oath. Read every field yourself.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Review every DS-160 answer yourself before submission. You are legally responsible for all content regardless of who prepared it.
blockers.rule_source_name: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent

blockers.title: DS-160 may not be consistent with supporting documents
blockers.user_message: Inconsistency between DS-160 and your documents reads as misrepresentation. Reconcile funding figures, employment, education dates, and family details before submitting.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Reconcile all DS-160 answers with your I-20, admission letter, and financial papers before submitting.
blockers.rule_source_name: DS-160 Online Application Must Be Completed and Consistent

blockers.title: No demonstrable ties to Pakistan
blockers.user_message: No ties = near-certain 214(b) refusal. Strongest ties are concrete: property in your name, a family business, a written career/job plan in Pakistan, assets. 'Parents live here' alone is weak.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Document at least one concrete tie — property, family business, written career plan, or financial assets in Pakistan.
blockers.rule_source_name: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)

blockers.title: Cannot specifically explain choice of USA and university
blockers.user_message: Generic answers sink interviews. Name the program, faculty, or specialization and tie it to your background and a Pakistan-based career. A random/agent-picked university is a 214(b) red flag.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Prepare a specific, personal explanation for why this university and programme connect to your background and career plans in Pakistan.
blockers.rule_source_name: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)

blockers.title: No clear career pathway back to Pakistan from this course
blockers.user_message: Show the path: your background -> this US program -> a named role/sector in Pakistan. No logical payoff at home signals immigration intent.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Be ready to state the specific role, sector, or employer in Pakistan this US programme prepares you for.
blockers.rule_source_name: Non-Immigrant Intent Must Be Demonstrated — Section 214(b)

blockers.title: Cannot explain sponsor funding in own words
blockers.user_message: Officers test whether YOU understand who pays and how they earned it. 'My uncle handles it' is weak. Know your sponsor's job, business, and how the money was accumulated.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Know your sponsor's job, business type, and how funds were accumulated. Officers test this directly.
blockers.rule_source_name: Interview Readiness — Consistent, Genuine, Unscripted Answers

blockers.title: Answers may appear rehearsed or scripted at interview
blockers.user_message: Officers spot rehearsed agent scripts instantly and it hurts credibility. Practise the content, but answer in your own words.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Practise your content but answer naturally in your own words. Scripted answers are easily identified and damage credibility.
blockers.rule_source_name: Interview Readiness — Consistent, Genuine, Unscripted Answers

blockers.title: Insufficient financial documents available
blockers.user_message: No documents = automatic financial credibility failure. Bring bank statements (6 months), sponsor income proof, FBR returns, and source-of-funds evidence.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Assemble bank statements, sponsor income proof, FBR returns, and source-of-funds evidence before the interview.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Bank statements do not show consistent balance history
blockers.user_message: A balance that appears suddenly before applying signals arranged funds. Consistent history over months is far stronger.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Ensure bank statements show a stable balance over at least 6 months. A sudden lump sum before applying is a credibility concern.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Source of funds not fully documented
blockers.user_message: Each major deposit needs proof: registered sale deed (property), FBR-declared salary, sanctioned loan letter, or a notarised gift affidavit from a traceable giver.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Provide documentary proof for every major deposit — sale deeds, salary slips, loan letters, or notarised gift affidavits.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Sponsor lacks FBR filing history consistent with funds
blockers.user_message: A sponsor showing big funds but non-filer/no FBR history is a major red flag — it implies undeclared income. Declared income should plausibly support the amount.
blockers.recommended_next_step: The sponsor's declared income should plausibly support the amount provided. Large undeclared funds raise credibility concerns.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Sponsor income cannot be proven with documentary evidence
blockers.user_message: Verbal claims aren't enough. Salary slips, business registration/NTN, FBR returns, and matching bank inflows make a sponsor credible.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Gather salary slips, business registration, NTN certificate, or FBR returns to make the sponsor's income credible.
blockers.rule_source_name: Financial Proof Must Cover Full Cost on the I-20

blockers.title: Education gap of over 12 months not evidenced
blockers.user_message: Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance proof, or transcripts covering the gap. Unevidenced 'I was at home/preparing' is weak and invites doubt at interview.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Provide employment letters, salary slips, freelance contracts, or academic transcripts covering the gap period.
blockers.rule_source_name: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)

blockers.title: Significant unexplained change of academic field
blockers.user_message: A big, unexplained field switch (e.g. completed Bachelors then an unrelated junior program) is a 214(b) trigger. If yes, be ready to explain the logic credibly.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Prepare a credible academic narrative explaining the field switch and its connection to your career plans in Pakistan.
blockers.rule_source_name: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)

blockers.title: Programme may represent an unexplained academic downgrade
blockers.user_message: Officers question progression that doesn't add up — e.g. a Masters-holder enrolling in a lower diploma. A downgrade looks like a visa-shopping move.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Ensure the US programme is a logical step forward from your existing qualification. Explain any apparent regression clearly.
blockers.rule_source_name: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)

blockers.title: Academic records may not be complete or verifiable
blockers.user_message: Inconsistent or unverifiable academics (mismatched names/dates, missing transcripts) raise fraud concerns. Have complete, attested records ready.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Have all transcripts and degrees verified, consistently named, and attested where required before the interview.
blockers.rule_source_name: Educational Consistency and Study-Plan Logic (214(b)-linked)

blockers.title: Prior visa refusal identified
blockers.user_message: Prior refusals are visible and probed. A refusal is survivable IF disclosed and explained — concealment on DS-160 is misrepresentation with a permanent-bar risk.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Disclose each refusal accurately on the DS-160 and prepare a clear explanation of what has changed since then.
blockers.rule_source_name: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed

blockers.title: Prior immigration breach (overstay or removal) identified
blockers.user_message: Overstays/removals strongly conflict with 'genuine temporary student' and must be disclosed and addressed candidly.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Disclose this history candidly on the DS-160 and at interview. Concealment is a misrepresentation ground.
blockers.rule_source_name: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed

blockers.title: Prior asylum claim identified
blockers.user_message: An asylum history conflicts with intent to return and must be addressed candidly, ideally with legal advice.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Disclose your asylum history fully. Consider seeking legal advice before applying given the impact on temporary-student intent.
blockers.rule_source_name: Prior Visa Refusals and Immigration Violations Must Be Disclosed

blockers.title: Agent has advised concealing information
blockers.user_message: If an agent told you to conceal something, that is a path to a misrepresentation bar. Disclose truthfully; drop the agent's advice.
blockers.recommended_next_step: Disclose everything accurately. Following advice to conceal information creates a permanent misrepresentation risk.
blockers.rule_source_name: Application Integrity and Agent Risk
